title: Price Check: Players Where Sites Disagree
brief: Which players have very different ranks or prices across sources, so their auction price in our room is hard to predict? Each line must say which direction the gap points and at what price the player becomes a buy for us.
summary: Most site gaps in our pool point one way: ESPN values sit far above Yahoo for players like Mitchell, Barnes, Davis, White and Bam, and the experts usually side with Yahoo or go even lower. A second group, including Alexander-Walker, Rollins, Garland, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lillard, has Yahoo and ESPN average costs well below expert value, and those are our best buys. Use expert value as the price cap, use average cost and ADP only to guess when a player will be nominated, and do not copy last season's prices from our room.

sections.heading: How to read a site gap

paragraphs.text: A rank or projection tells you how good a player is. ADP and average cost are the market price. They tell you when he is likely to be available. If you rank a player 30th and his ADP is 70th, you can wait and take him in the 50s. In our auction that means your bid cap comes from your value, and the market tells you how hard you will have to fight for him.

ADP and average cost are averages, not medians. A player with ADP 50 goes after pick 50 in only about half of drafts, and he often goes earlier than the number suggests. So do not plan to wait until his average cost if you really want him. Bid up to your cap the first time he is nominated.

Yahoo, ESPN and Fantrax rank players very differently. Whether a player is a bust or a steal depends on platform and format. We are a Yahoo 9-cat auction room, so an ESPN rank or a points-league view is only a hint for us. Our own room's prices from last season are a third reference point, but several have aged badly. Booker went for 45 USD and Davis for 54 USD, and experts now price both far lower.

Yahoo auction price data differs a lot from snake-draft ADP data, so treat the two separately. For us, Yahoo auction average cost is the most relevant market signal. Snake ADP mainly tells you about hype. Castle is a clear case: his Yahoo ADP is about 56, but experts fade him there and his category value is much lower.

A Yahoo ADP based on very few drafts can be inflated. Some Yahoo ADPs are also skewed by dynasty leagues where a player is drafted in only a small share of leagues, so ignore those. Before 2026-10-18, check the draft count behind any Yahoo ADP that looks odd. Edgecombe has a Yahoo ADP around 63 against an ESPN ADP of 112. Experts still price him near 10 USD, so do not chase his Yahoo ADP.

Yahoo's own value and Yahoo's average cost can also be far apart. Alexander-Walker has a 17 USD Yahoo value but a 4 USD average cost. Rollins has a 17 USD value but a 2 USD average cost. For these players the gap is a buying chance, not a warning.

sections.heading: ESPN is high: let others pay

paragraphs.text: The most common gap has ESPN well above Yahoo, with experts siding with Yahoo or going lower. ESPN values Mitchell at 59 USD, but experts see 31 to 40 USD. ESPN puts Barnes at 55 USD, but experts plan on 31 to 35 USD. ESPN puts Edwards at 60 USD, but experts say 40 to 45 USD. ESPN's rank of 15 for Davis is called too high because of his games played, so stop in the mid 20s USD.

The same pattern holds lower in the pool. Experts call ESPN's 43 USD for Bam far too high and price him in the mid 20s. White is 42 USD on ESPN but a mid 20s player to the experts. Kawhi is 40 USD on ESPN, but experts cap him at 24 USD. Siakam, Bridges and Allen are also ranked much higher on ESPN than experts see them. If a manager in our room bids from ESPN numbers, let him have these players.

sections.heading: Yahoo is high: wait for the discount

paragraphs.text: A smaller group has Yahoo above ESPN, and the experts lean toward ESPN. Holmgren is 29 USD on Yahoo against an expert price of 21 to 22 USD. Kessler is 25 USD on Yahoo, but experts aim for 12 to 15 USD. Clingan's Yahoo average cost is 16.2 USD, but experts say 7 to 10 USD. Sarr is 18 USD on Yahoo, but experts see a pick 80 to 90 player. Zubac is 18 USD on Yahoo, but experts cap him near 14 USD. Several of these are big men, so plan your center spot with a cheaper option in mind.

Some guards and forwards fit here too. Trae is 38 USD on Yahoo, and experts call the ESPN average cost of about 33 USD closer to fair. Durant's Yahoo average cost of 49.6 USD is a stretch, and a price in the low 40s is fair. Wagner's 21 USD Yahoo value is above the experts' 11 to 15 USD.

sections.heading: Both markets too low: plan to buy

paragraphs.text: When a player's ESPN ADP is far later than his rank, drafters are passing on him round after round, so grab him when that happens in your draft. In our room, take these players as soon as the price drops below your cap. Alexander-Walker is supported up to about 20 USD. Garland is fair at 20 to 25 USD. Jaren Jackson Jr. is a strong buy in the high teens. Rollins is a top 50 player who costs about 2 USD on both sites.

Other experts' buys at market price include Lillard at 5 to 10 USD, Paul George up to his 13 USD Yahoo value, Buzelis at 15 to 22 USD, Keyonte George at 15 to 20 USD and Daniels at 18 to 24 USD. Jamal Murray has the reverse gap: Yahoo buyers pay about 39 USD and ESPN buyers about 25 USD. Experts rank him above both sites, so the mid to high 30s is still fair.

The experts do not always agree on these prices. For Amen Thompson, most experts value him at 35 to 40 USD, but Lloyd calls him only a third-round pick if his blocks and FG% do not come back. Edey went for 20 USD in a mock while Josh capped him at 11 USD. Knueppel sold for 13 USD against Josh's limit of 8 USD. In each case, our cap sits at the lower expert number unless early-season news supports the higher one. Big gaps between sites also cut both ways. One view says a late ESPN ADP is a signal to grab the player. The other says platform data should be read separately, because rankings differ by platform and format.
